observation_summary: BigFraction.doubleValue() and floatValue() return NaN for fractions with very large numerators or denominators, even when the resulting quotient is within the valid range of a double or float.
reasoning_summary: The bug occurs because BigInteger.doubleValue() and BigInteger.floatValue() return Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY or Double.NaN when the BigInteger magnitude exceeds the range of a double or float. In the original implementation, the code directly divided these values, leading to NaN results (e.g., Infinity/Infinity) even when the actual fraction value was well within the representable range of a double or float. The fix introduces a fallback mechanism that detects when the initial division results in NaN and shifts the bits of the numerator and denominator to scale them down into a range where the division can be performed accurately.
